asks: What does the record do when a computer floods it?
answer: A flood coarsens the present and never erases the past. Under pressure, a source merges new lines before writing them (per folder, per host). A merge never mixes facts with reports, and it is marked as a merge. Lines already written are never changed. Older ones are not evicted to make room, because an agent could then erase its trail by making noise.

sets.says: A flood from one computer never removes older facts and reports.
